newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM urges "no caving in to terrorism" in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM urges "no caving in to terrorism" in Peru.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday he would use an emergency weekend meeting with Peru's president to confirm there would be no "caving in to terrorism" in solving the Lima hostage crisis.

Hashimoto and Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori plan to meet in Toronto on Saturday to discuss the six-week standoff at the Japanese ambassador's residence, where leftist guerrillas are holding 72 captives.

"I can't go into details at this delicate stage but what we must confirm is that we must not cave in to terrorism and at the same time seek the release of all captives unharmed and as soon as possible," Hashimoto told a parliamentary committee.

The meeting, which follows telephone conversations in which Hashimoto asked Fujimori to avoid provoking the Marxist rebels, is a sign of growing concern in Lima and Tokyo that the crisis shows no signs of ending.

Hashimoto has told Fujimori that Japan is worried that the hostages' lives could be endangered if pressure is stepped up on the roughly 15 armed members of the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
In an apparent bid to weaken the rebels' resolve, police have blasted marching music at the residence in the early morning and led processions of armoured vehicles around it.
The rebels, who have mined and booby-trapped the diplomatic residence, fired several bullets on Monday at police in a convoy of armoured cars, hitting one vehicle.
